question: Describe the Shoplifting to Burglary transition in anomaly/Shoplifting/Shoplifting034_x264.mp4 around 166 seconds.

correlations.description: Compatible Shoplifting hypotheses persist across adjacent windows from 162.133s-164.133s to 164.267s-166.267s with co-occurring suitcase detections and garbage collecting labels.
The Shoplifting hypothesis window ending at 166.267s occurs before the Burglary hypothesis window starting at 166.4s.
All three evidence records belong to the same Phase 2D incident anomaly/Shoplifting/Shoplifting034_x264.mp4:i0.

Object detections for person and suitcase co-occur in the same windows as surveillance-event hypotheses and generic-action labels, indicating source co-occurrence only and not confirmation of involvement.

inferences.text: The available evidence suggests a change in model output from Shoplifting hypotheses before 166.267s to a Burglary hypothesis starting at 166.4s, consistent with a transition in hypotheses around 166 seconds, without establishing that crimes occurred or that detected persons were involved.

The evidence is consistent with persistent activity labeled as garbage collecting across the interval with confidence increasing from 0.3742 to 0.8296, but model agreement does not confirm the nature of the activity.

limitations: Reasoning is limited to supplied evidence without access to footage; model labels are hypotheses, not confirmed crimes.
Temporal gaps between windows (164.133s-164.267s and 166.267s-166.4s) are unobserved and activity during gaps cannot be determined.
Person and object detections overlapping hypotheses do not indicate involvement, and identities, roles, or causation cannot be determined.
